title: Two Surfaces, Two Environments: Dev/Prod Parity — Check

questions.prompt: Why does the Agronomy Studio frontend talk to only two surfaces (the gateway and the mock AI search)?
questions.explanation: A minimal surface (two URLs with fixed shapes) can be reproduced by a local mock, enabling offline development and a fast inner loop.
options: To reduce the number of HTTP libraries the frontend must bundle
Because a small, stable surface is easy to reproduce locally for development
Because Netlify only allows two redirect rules
To make the UI render faster in the browser

questions.prompt: For dev/prod parity to be useful, the local mock and the production function must return identical values, not just identical response shapes.
questions.explanation: Parity is about matching the response *shape*/schema so bugs reproduce. The actual values will differ (real weather vs. fixture data); that is expected.

questions.prompt: What does the URL path `/agronomy-api/soil` represent in this architecture?
questions.explanation: The path is the shared contract. Whatever answers it — local mock or Netlify function — must honor the same request/response shape, making the implementation swappable.
options: A hard-coded link to the CIMIS upstream service
The contract that both the local mock and the production function must satisfy
A redirect that only exists in production
A frontend-only route with no backend behind it
